examples.source: HIGH COURT OF JUDICATURE AT Madras. Criminal Miscellaneous Application No. 3237 of 2020. The applicant Suresh Pawar seeks anticipatory bail under Section 438 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 in Crime No. 308/2020, registered under Sections 409 and 420 of the Indian Penal Code, for misappropriating ₹25.5 crore collected from 174 investors between 14 July 2020 and 6 October 2020. Custodial interrogation is necessary to trace the money. The application is rejected. The interim protection granted on 8 December 2020 stands vacated, and the applicant shall surrender before the investigating officer within 9 days.

Translation, price-matched cloud tier (120 items each): openai:gpt-5.4-mini kept 99.9% of facts (0.008 lost per passage) and claude-haiku-5.5 kept 99.9% (0.017). Both are slightly ahead of gemini-3.8-flash (99.8%) and sarvam-105b (99.6%), and none added unsupported numbers. Frontier models on the fixed 30 items (first 15 passages x hi/ta): gpt-5.5 100%, claude-sonnet-5.5 99.8%, gemini-pro-latest 99.8%. On that same subset, sarvam-translate scored 99.5% and sarvam-105b 99.3%. Translation is close to solved for every system except mayura.

Litigant summaries, key-fact recall:
- Price-matched tier (80 items each): gpt-5.4-mini 97.5%, claude-haiku-5.5 97.3%, gemini-3.8-flash 98.3%; none invented numbers.
- Frontier, same 30 items: gpt-5.5 100%, claude-sonnet-5.5 100%, gemini-pro-latest 97.8%.
- On those 30 items, sarvam-105b scored 84.4% with think off and 92.8% with think on (reruns included).
So the Sarvam API is the only cloud option that leaves out roughly 1 in 7 key facts.

The OpenAI models sometimes answer in mixed Hindi-English: gpt-5.4-mini in 1 of 80 summaries and gpt-5.5 in 1 of 30. They keep court names, 'Criminal Complaint No.' and party names in Latin script, so less than 50% of the letters are Devanagari. That fails the language check even though the facts are all there.

Latency p50: translation gpt-5.4-mini 2.0 s, claude-haiku 3.5 s, claude-sonnet 5.3 s, gpt-5.5 14 s, gemini-pro 23 s. Summaries gpt-5.4-mini 2.0 s, haiku 3.5 s, sonnet 8.5 s, gpt-5.5 9.6 s, gemini-pro 16 s.
caveats: The passages are synthetic: 12 templates filled 40 times, so errors are correlated within a template. Real judgments are longer, messier and full of citations. The source is always English.

Scoring checks whether entities survive, not meaning. Swapped party roles, wrong outcomes (bail granted or rejected) and negations are not caught. Spot checks found such errors (mayura calling both parties 'accused'). The examples in this file show full outputs.

The name check is a heuristic: a consonant skeleton with fuzzy matching (see score.py). Correct Tamil spellings that write h as க (சவுகான் for Chauhan) are missed, and modernised place names (Madras to சென்னை, Bombay to मुंबई) count as altered. Both affect every system. Amounts written fully in words are not credited.
The LLMs were told to keep numbers and write names in the target script. The translate APIs cannot take instructions and ran with defaults (formal mode, international numerals).
Think-on ran with max_tokens 6000. With a larger budget it would return fewer empty replies, at higher cost and latency.

The local-model results rest on 10 items and are indicative only. Their latency reflects a shared machine running other jobs. sarvam-30b-local's reasoning leak may come from the llama.cpp chat-template setup rather than the model.
Back-translation was not run. Translation fluency and legal register were not measured.

Frontier models ran only on a fixed 30-item subset per task (first 15 passages x Hindi/Tamil), with think on at provider-default effort. OpenAI prices are not recorded; OpenRouter cost is what usage.cost reported.
verdict: For translating court orders, RTI replies and tribunal awards into Hindi, Tamil, Marathi or Bengali, gemini-3.8-flash, sarvam-105b (think off) and sarvam-translate:v1 all keep about 99.5% or more of the facts. Hindi is essentially solved, and Tamil is where they differ. If you want a Sarvam stack, prefer sarvam-105b: it matched sarvam-translate on facts at roughly 1/80th of the list cost per passage. Do not use mayura:v1 for legal or financial text: it loses about one fact in every two passages and garbles decimal crore amounts (₹25.5 crore became 5 crore). For plain-language litigant summaries, every non-Sarvam cloud model tested (gemini-3.8-flash, gpt-5.4-mini, claude-haiku-5.5, and the frontier tier on its subset) is clearly better: 98% of key facts and no invented numbers, against 85% and 9% of summaries with unsupported numbers for sarvam-105b. If you use sarvam-105b, either keep thinking off or give it at least 16k max_tokens (89% recall at about 20x the tokens and 21 s); tell it not to compute dates or totals, and check every number in the output against the source before it reaches a litigant. Self-hosted, qwen3-30b did better than sarvam-30b on this small sample.
